title: 参考 · 皮层分层与微回路 — 神经科学

questions.question: 研究者只知道一条皮层间连接的终止层：它落在 L4，而 L1 和 L5/6 几乎没有。按分层规则，这条连接更可能是什么？
options: 前馈连接，从层级较低的区域送往较高的区域
丘脑发出的调制性输入，主要用于调节注意
反馈连接，从层级较高的区域送回较低的区域
同一区域内的横向连接，不分层级的上下
questions.explanation: Felleman 和 Van Essen 正是用落点来定层级：前馈从 L2/3 出发、终止在 L4；反馈从深层出发、避开 L4，落在 L1 和 L5/6。丘脑的调制性输入落在 L1，本地横向连接最密的是 L2/3。
questions.question_en: All a researcher knows about a corticocortical connection is where it ends: in L4, with almost nothing in L1 or L5/6. By the laminar rule, what is it most likely to be?
options_en: A feedforward connection, from a lower-level area to a higher-level one
A modulatory input from the thalamus, mainly used to regulate attention
A feedback connection, from a higher-level area back to a lower one
A lateral connection within one area, with no up or down in the hierarchy
questions.explanation_en: Felleman and Van Essen used termination layers to build the hierarchy: feedforward projections start in L2/3 and end in L4, while feedback starts in deep layers, avoids L4, and lands in L1 and L5/6. Modulatory thalamic input lands in L1, and local lateral connections are densest in L2/3.

questions.question: 关于皮层锥体细胞的两头，下列哪个说法正确？
options: 顶端树突只接收抑制性输入，作用是给细胞降噪，兴奋性的前馈与反馈都只落在基底树突上
基底树突收本地与前馈输入，顶端在 L1 接反馈；顶端被强驱动时细胞转为连放
基底树突在 L1 接住反馈，顶端树突收本地和前馈输入；两路输入在胞体处简单相加后统一输出
顶端和基底树突收的都是前馈输入，只是距离胞体远近不同，所以两头之间没有功能上的分工
questions.explanation: 基底树突短而密，围在胞体旁收本地与前馈输入；顶端树突伸到 L1 展开，接远处反馈。两头不是简单相加：顶端被足够强地驱动时会转成连放，下游借此读出「上面那一路刚才有没有说话」。也有中间神经元专门压顶端，但顶端并非只收抑制。
questions.question_en: Which statement about the two ends of a cortical pyramidal cell is correct?
options_en: Apical dendrites receive only inhibitory input to denoise the cell, while excitatory feedforward and feedback both land on basal dendrites
Basal dendrites take local and feedforward input, apical dendrites receive feedback in L1, and strong apical drive switches the cell from single spikes to bursts
Basal dendrites receive feedback in L1, apical dendrites take local and feedforward input, and the two streams simply sum at the soma
Both apical and basal dendrites take feedforward input and differ only in distance from the soma, so the two ends have no division of labor
questions.explanation_en: Basal dendrites are short and dense around the soma, collecting local and feedforward input; the apical dendrite reaches L1 and fans out to receive long-range feedback. The two don't just add up: strong enough apical drive switches the cell to bursting, so downstream cells can tell whether the top-down stream just spoke. Some interneurons do target the apical tuft, but it isn't inhibitory-only.
